Subject: Order form invoice recipient & tax evidence — path of record

Hi Anna / Medivex team,

Following up on our call yesterday — attaching the latest order form (OrderForm_v3) and a clean invoice flow diagram so procurement can confirm the actual invoice recipient. Two items we need to lock before legal signs the MSA/order form: 

1) Invoice recipient: we need confirmation whether Medivex will accept invoices to Medivex Health, Inc. (US entity) or to the EU subsidiary (Medivex EU). This impacts withholding and VAT handling.
2) Tax evidence: when you confirm the recipient, please also share the tax docs you typically require (VAT registration or US W-9) and whether you need gross-up language on taxes.

We can accept either recipient but it affects net terms (we typically do net30 for US entities; EU customers sometimes request net45 with VAT reverse-charge). If Medivex requires the invoice to go to Medivex EU, we’ll need the VAT number before invoice issuance.

I’ve cc’d Ben (billing/finance) and Lauren (contracts) so they can validate downstream ops and PO routing. If you can reply with: (a) invoice recipient entity name and remit address, and (b) required tax evidence, we’ll mark the order form ready for legal to sign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if that’s easier.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: invoice_flow_diagram.png (image)

Team — forwarding Medivex redlines. Key asks: invoice recipient confirmed as Medivex Health, Inc. (US) + W-9 forthcoming. Procurement asks for two negotiable items: (1) 60-day pre-approval language for invoices older than 60 days, and (2) optional net45 for >$250k ARR.

Ben: can you confirm if we can support net45 for this deal size from a cashflow/AR perspective? If not, what's the compromise (e.g., net30 + 45-day approval cadence)? Also please confirm the invoice remittance flow if invoice goes to the US entity (PO -> AR system -> wire).

Karthik / Lauren: procurement wants the 60-day pre-approval clause in the billing appendix. Legal flagged that the clause should not create an indefinite holdback on payment liability; we can propose language that requires written AP approval for any invoice older than 60 days, and if no response within 30 days, invoice is considered undisputed. Thoughts on acceptable language?

Suggest we do a short sync (15–20m) first thing Fri to finalize language and respond to Anna with a tracked-change version.

—Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order form invoice recipient & tax evidence — path of record

Kimberly / team — quick ops check after reviewing the redlines and cashflow model:

1) Net terms: cashflow modeling says we can accept net45 on this specific contract if Medivex signs a 12-month minimum commit at the quoted ARR (DEAL-3491). Otherwise standard net30 stands. Recommend we offer the conditional net45 ("Net45 subject to 12-month committed ARR >= $250k"), and include a clause that if receipts fall below 80% of forecast after 90 days, terms revert to net30 for future invoices.

2) 60-day pre-approval: Ben suggests alternate language: "Invoices older than 60 days require written AP clarification; such invoices will be marked for review and payment may be deferred pending written confirmation. Absent written dispute within 30 days of notice, invoices shall be considered undisputed and payable under the agreed net terms." This preserves buyer protection without indefinite hold. Legal should sign off on tightening.

3) Attachments needed for PO execution: once Anna returns the W-9 we need the purchase order number and remit address exactly as it will appear on the PO. Finance will not process without a PO number.

I can join the Friday sync. If Karthik / Lauren can draft tracked change language for both items, I’ll push the conditional net45 into the billing appendix and flag for AR workflow.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
